page: Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and features 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Additionally, it includes 410 GB of local storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the E16a_v4 in the average tier for most multi-threaded and memory-bound workloads. While its single-core CPU performance is rated as poor in stress-ng tests, its multi-core execution and Geekbench scores align with the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory read bandwidth is average at 52.1 GB/sec for large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth is weaker, measuring at 25.51 GB/sec. The server demonstrates stable performance for database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, but exhibits limitations in demanding tasks like medium-sized LLM inference.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16a_v4 offers a high-density memory configuration on a dedicated AMD EPYC platform, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require top-tier single-core compute speeds. The inclusion of 410 GB of local storage adds value for temporary data caching. This server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
